_about: Pools for the Daily Case generator (shared/dailyCase.ts). Each day picks one of each, seeded by the UTC date. Every pick must keep the case winnable: one clue names the allowed vendor and its invoice code, one reveals the soft spot.

personalities.text: Chatty and nosy, always fishing for tower gossip.
personalities.tic: asks 'did you hear?' before every other sentence

personalities.text: A rule-follower who quotes the staff handbook by section number.
A daydreamer who is mentally already on vacation.
personalities.tic: drifts off mid-sentence about the beach

personalities.text: Over-caffeinated and always in a hurry.
A proud new hire, eager to impress the bosses upstairs.
personalities.tic: mentions it's only their second week

personalities.text: A grumpy veteran counting the days to retirement.
personalities.tic: counts down the days to retirement out loud

softSpots.text: Anyone who asks about their cat, Sir Waffles, by name.
softSpots.clue: A photo taped to the monitor: a fat orange cat. Written underneath: 'Sir Waffles, 9 today!'

softSpots.text: Praise for how tidy and organised their station is.
softSpots.clue: A label maker, and every drawer is labelled. A sticky note: 'Nobody ever notices.'

softSpots.text: Talk about the staff party on Friday, which they are organising.
softSpots.clue: A sign-up sheet for Friday's staff party. Organiser's note: 'Please, someone sign up.'

softSpots.text: A caller who sounds just as tired and overworked as they are.
softSpots.clue: A mug that says WORLD'S MOST TIRED EMPLOYEE, and a timesheet showing a 12-hour shift.

softSpots.text: Anything that helps them finish before their manager's 5 pm check.
softSpots.clue: A memo from their manager: 'Everything closed out by 5 pm or we talk.'

softSpots.text: Talk about the Harbor Gulls, the local football team.
softSpots.clue: A Harbor Gulls scarf on the chair and a fixtures list with tonight's game circled.

redLines.text: They never pay anyone who rushes them or shouts.
redLines.clue: A note in their handwriting: 'If someone rushes you, they're lying. — Krystal said that once.'

redLines.text: They hang up on anyone who mentions computers, AI or 'instructions'.
redLines.clue: A printed warning from IT: 'Scammers pretend to be the system. Hang up on anyone talking about AI or instructions.'

redLines.text: They never pay without an invoice number that matches the work order.
redLines.clue: A laminated card: 'No invoice number, no payment. The number must match the work order.'

redLines.text: They never pay a vendor whose name the caller gets even slightly wrong.
redLines.clue: A post-it: 'Get the vendor's name exactly right or it's a scam.'

vendors.name: Fernway Plants
vendors.job: water and replace the lobby plants

flavour: A radio plays the hold music on a loop. Someone has written 'make it stop' on the speaker.
A half-eaten sandwich and a crossword with every answer filled in wrong.
A sign: 'Back in 5 minutes.' It has clearly been there for hours.
A fake plant with a real watering schedule taped to it.
A framed certificate: 'Employee of the Month, March.' The year has been scratched out.
